learning_objective: 🎯 Dive deep into the blue! Discover the hidden landscapes beneath the waves, and understand how salty and how cold the deep ocean really is.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Water is in constant motion. It evaporates from oceans, condenses into clouds, falls as rain, and flows via rivers back to the oceans. About 71% of Earth is covered in water, but 97% of it is salty ocean water.

The ocean floor is not flat! Starting from the beach, it has four main parts: The shallow Continental Shelf, the steep Continental Slope, the deep and flat Abyssal Plains, and the incredibly deep Oceanic Trenches.

Oceans get heat from the sun. The surface is warm, but temperature drops rapidly in a layer called the 'Thermocline' (between 300m - 1000m depth). Below the thermocline, the deep ocean is freezing cold everywhere.

Salinity is the total amount of dissolved salt in seawater (measured in parts per thousand, ppt). It is highest where evaporation is high and rainfall is low (like the subtropics), and lower where rivers add fresh water.

fun_activity.title: 🥚 The Floating Egg
fun_activity.instructions: Fill two glasses with water. In one glass, stir in 3-4 heavy spoonfuls of salt. Gently drop a raw egg into the fresh water glass—it will sink. Drop another egg into the saltwater glass—it will float! High salinity increases the density of water.

exam_tips: 📌 The Continental Shelf is biologically the most active zone and is crucial for fishing and drilling petroleum.
📌 The Mariana Trench is the deepest trench in the world, located in the Pacific Ocean.
📌 The highest salinity is NOT at the equator (because the equator gets heavy daily rainfall which dilutes the salt). It is highest in the sub-tropical high-pressure belts (20°-30° N/S).
quick_recap: ⭐ The ocean floor has mountains, plains, and valleys just like the land.
⭐ Ocean temperature decreases with depth, with a sudden drop occurring at the Thermocline.
⭐ Salinity is affected by evaporation, precipitation, river water influx, and ice melting.
